_readme: This file is the single source of truth for every event on the site.
from here through the loader in app.py.
IMPORTANT — UNVERIFIED FACTS ARE INTENTIONALLY BLANK.
date, start_time, end_time, venue and prizes are EMPTY strings because
no confirmed dates, venues or prize amounts have been supplied by the
project owner. The interface renders a clear 'To be confirmed' state
instead of inventing details. Fill them in when the details are known
category           used for the category filter (no invented categories)
short_description  one or two lines, shown on cards
description        full description, shown on the event page
venue              location string or '' when not confirmed
min_team_size      1 for a purely individual event
max_team_size      upper limit for a team
milestones        optional session list for the event

events.title: Prompt Wars
events.short_description: An AI prompt-engineering battle judged on output quality, control and originality.
events.description: Prompt Wars is an AI & Automation competition about writing instructions that a generative model can actually follow. Teams receive a themed brief, then craft and refine the prompts that produce the strongest result. A live head-to-head round follows, where a team has a short window to repair its prompt after seeing a rival's output. Judging looks at relevance, structure, completeness, creativity and control — and at the prompt itself, not only the output.
events.eligibility: Open to all students of the participating institution. No department restriction.
events.team_requirements: A team may enter alone or with one partner.
rules: Only the AI tool and interface supplied by the organisers may be used.
External browser tabs, offline documents and pre-written prompt libraries are not permitted.
Every prompt used in the judged rounds must be submitted for review.
The live round is timed; prompts submitted late are not scored.
Copying another team's prompt or output results in disqualification.
Judging follows the published rubric and the decision is final.

highlights.title: Prompt design
highlights.text: Write precise, layered instructions that steer the model towards a defined goal.

highlights.title: Iteration
highlights.text: Critique an output and rewrite the prompt so the next answer is measurably better.

highlights.title: Live duel
highlights.text: Repair and improve your prompt in a short, timed head-to-head round.

highlights.title: Rubric judging
highlights.text: Scored on relevance, structure, creativity and how much control you demonstrated.

events.title: Debugging
events.short_description: A live debugging sprint on broken code — identify the fault, explain it and repair it.
events.description: Debugging is a Software Engineering competition built around real bug-hunting. Each team receives a listing containing a deliberately injected set of errors and must identify every fault, write the corrected version, and explain to the judges why the original code failed. Rounds increase in difficulty from a short warm-up snippet to a full mini-program. Partial credit is awarded per fault found, with a separate explanation score that separates teams that guess the fix from teams that understand it.
events.eligibility: Open to students of the participating institution, with no restriction on year of study.
events.team_requirements: Individual or pair entry. The registered size must match the entry type.
rules: A plain text editor is provided; no IDE, autocomplete or internet access is allowed.
Each round contains a fixed number of injected faults and partial credit is given per fault.
The corrected code is judged on correctness first and clarity of explanation second.
Writing on the question paper is not permitted.
The judge may ask any team member to explain any part of the answer.
Time is strictly monitored and answers are collected at the signal.

highlights.title: Bug identification
highlights.text: Read unfamiliar code and pin-point every injected fault quickly.

highlights.title: Code correction
highlights.text: Rewrite the snippet so that it compiles and behaves as intended.

highlights.title: Explanation round
highlights.text: Justify the fix to the judges in front of the panel.

highlights.title: Score review
highlights.text: Per-fault scores and explanation scores are read out together.

events.title: UI/UX
events.short_description: A design thinking sprint — problem framing, wireframes, prototype and a judged pitch.
events.description: UI/UX runs like a miniature product design sprint. Teams are given a real problem to work on and must move from problem framing all the way to a clickable prototype. The submission includes a short problem statement, user personas, low and high fidelity wireframes, a working prototype, and a short pitch to the judges. Scoring covers problem understanding, research quality, visual hierarchy, usability reasoning and how convincingly the team defends its design decisions.
events.eligibility: Open to all students of the participating institution.
events.team_requirements: Teams of two to four. A mix of design and development skills is encouraged.
rules: A team must have two to four members and must nominate a presenting lead.
The brief provided by the organisers is the only accepted problem statement.
The submission must include wireframes, a working prototype and a pitch.
The prototype must be demonstrated live; static images alone are not accepted.
Pitch length and question time are fixed and announced before the event.
Copying another team's work or assets is not allowed.
Judging follows the published rubric and the decision is final.

highlights.title: Design thinking
highlights.text: Define the problem, research users and frame a clear design challenge.

highlights.title: Wireframing
highlights.text: Sketch low fidelity layouts, then upgrade to high fidelity screens.

highlights.title: Prototyping
highlights.text: Build a clickable flow that demonstrates the core experience.

highlights.title: Design pitch
highlights.text: Present the work and defend every design decision.

events.title: Ideathon
events.short_description: An innovation challenge to pitch an original, practical solution to a stated problem.
events.description: Ideathon is the flagship Innovation competition. Teams are given a live problem statement and a limited working window to design a solution around it. The submission must be original, feasible within a realistic timeframe and connected to a real need. Each team presents to the panel and then answers questions from it. A written submission with a rough implementation sketch is retained for an exhibition showcase alongside the festival.
events.eligibility: Open to all students of the participating institution.
events.team_requirements: Teams of two to four, with at least one member from a technical discipline.
rules: A team must have two to four members, including at least one technical-discipline student.
The problem statement is announced at the start and no external problem lists are allowed.
Working time is limited to the announced duration and is strictly monitored.
Ideas must be original and must not reproduce a commercially released product.
Pitch length and question time are fixed and enforced by the timekeeper.
A written submission with an implementation sketch is required for the showcase.
Judging follows the published rubric and the decision is final.

highlights.title: Problem framing
highlights.text: Understand the live problem and define who exactly the solution serves.

highlights.title: Idea generation
highlights.text: Brainstorm broadly, then converge on one defensible concept.

highlights.title: Feasibility check
highlights.text: Sketch the implementation plan, the team needs and a realistic timeline.

highlights.title: Stage pitch
highlights.text: Deliver the pitch, then answer the panel.

events.title: IT Quiz
events.short_description: A two-stage quiz spanning programming, hardware, networking and tech trivia.
events.description: IT Quiz tests breadth and speed across the whole information technology spectrum — programming languages, data structures, operating systems, computer networks, databases, security basics, current trends and well-known figures from the industry. The quiz runs in two stages: a written prelim, followed by a buzzer round projected on the main screen with rapid-fire questions. Teams enter as a pair.
events.eligibility: Open to all students of the participating institution.
rules: A team must have exactly two registered members and both must be present for the prelim.
The prelim is a fixed number of questions under a fixed time limit; negative marking applies as published.
The top teams from the prelim qualify for the buzzer round.
Electronic devices other than the buzzer are prohibited in the final round.
Once a team answers, the answer is locked and cannot be changed.
Ties are broken by the earliest buzzer press in the deciding question.
The judges' decision on a disputed question is final.

highlights.title: Written prelim
highlights.text: A timed paper covering the full information technology spectrum.

highlights.title: Buzzer round
highlights.text: Audio-visual rapid questions on the stage screen.

highlights.title: Rapid negatives
highlights.text: A short negative-marking sprint that decides the tie breakers.

highlights.title: Result reading
highlights.text: Placing teams are announced and photographed on stage.

events.title: Paper Presentation
events.short_description: A conference-style paper presentation judged on research depth and delivery.
events.description: Paper Presentation is modelled on a small student conference. Teams submit an original technical or interdisciplinary paper and then present it to a review panel. The paper is judged on the depth of the research, correctness of the technical content, literature review, methodology and the quality of the presentation itself. Each team receives a fixed speaking slot followed by a question round from the panel, and written feedback is returned to every team afterwards.
events.eligibility: Open to all students of the participating institution.
events.team_requirements: Individual entry, or teams of up to three. The presenting author must be a registered member.
rules: The paper must be original work and must not have been published or submitted elsewhere.
The paper must be submitted before the deadline stated by the organisers.
The paper must follow the shared template and stay within the published page range.
The speaking slot and the question round are fixed and strictly enforced.
Slide count is limited and must match the content of the paper.
The presenting author must be one of the registered members.
The panel's evaluation and feedback are final.

highlights.title: Research
highlights.text: Investigate the problem and review the existing literature properly.

highlights.title: Technical writing
highlights.text: Present methodology, results and conclusions in the shared paper format.

highlights.title: Slide design
highlights.text: Turn the paper into a clear, visual story that fits the slot.

highlights.title: Panel questions
highlights.text: Defend the research against a question round from the reviewers.

events.title: Free Fire
events.short_description: A squad tournament in Clash Squad mode, played on organiser-supplied devices.
events.description: Free Fire is a Gaming & Esports team tournament played on mobile devices supplied by the organisers. Squads are seeded into a single-elimination bracket and play a fixed number of rounds, with every round requiring a full squad. Organisers run the matches on a LAN-enabled station and publish the results after each round. The winning squad is announced on stage.
events.eligibility: Open to all students of the participating institution.
events.team_requirements: Squads of exactly four with one nominated captain.
rules: A squad must have exactly four registered members; substitutes are not permitted once registration closes.
Squad names must be unique and must not contain abusive language.
All matches are played on the official organiser-supplied devices and tournament build.
Players must report to the assigned station before the first round.
Devices must be charged to at least the published minimum level.
Third-party applications, emulators and external communication during a match lead to disqualification.
Hardware failure is resolved by the referee's decision, which is final.

highlights.title: Squad check-in
highlights.text: Verify the four-player roster and collect the assigned device.

highlights.title: Bracket battles
highlights.text: Play through elimination rounds against the other seeded squads.

highlights.title: Live standings
highlights.text: Follow every round on the organiser's public bracket display.

highlights.title: Closing ceremony
highlights.text: The winning squad is announced on stage.

events.title: BGMI
events.short_description: A squad tournament in Battlegrounds Mobile India on organiser-supplied devices.
events.description: BGMI is the second Gaming & Esports tournament, run in squad mode on organiser-supplied devices with the organiser's ruleset applied. Squads are seeded into a single-elimination bracket and play through several rounds in custom rooms. The last squad standing is declared the winner. Each squad is allotted a fixed station slot and a device check-in time, and spectators can follow the bracket on the organiser's display.
events.eligibility: Open to all students of the participating institution.
events.team_requirements: Squads of exactly four with one nominated captain.
rules: A squad must have exactly four registered members; the roster is verified at the station desk.
Only organiser-provided devices and the official tournament build may be used.
Device check-in begins before the first round and slot swaps are not permitted.
Bans, third-party applications and external voice communication during a match are prohibited.
Any disconnection is handled by the referee's ruling, which is final.
Squad names must be unique across the tournament.
A player may not take part in two gaming events on the same day.

highlights.title: Roster check-in
highlights.text: Verify the four-player roster and collect the assigned device.

highlights.title: Bracket rounds
highlights.text: Fight through single-elimination rounds in custom rooms.

highlights.title: Live bracket
highlights.text: Track every round on the organiser's public display.

highlights.title: Closing ceremony
highlights.text: The winning squad is announced on stage.

events.title: IPL Auction
events.short_description: A virtual cricket auction where teams bid on a player pool with a fixed purse.
events.description: IPL Auction puts participants in the shoes of a franchise owner. Every team receives a virtual purse and a pool of players across several tiers, and must build a balanced squad while staying inside the purse ceiling. The auction is conducted live with a projected price board. Squad quality is scored after the auction on a balanced-squad formula: roles covered, quality of the top order, bowling depth, and how little of the purse is wasted.
events.eligibility: Open to all students of the participating institution.
events.team_requirements: Teams of two or three, with one member nominated as the manager who places the bids.
rules: A team must have two or three members and exactly one nominated auction manager.
Every team receives a fixed virtual purse and must complete a valid squad within it.
Only the nominated manager may place a bid; other members may advise but not bid.
Bids below the reserve price are rejected automatically.
A team that exceeds its purse is disqualified from the squad-scoring round.
Only registered players from the provided pool may be bought.
All monetary values are virtual; no real money is involved at any stage.
Decisions are final once the auction is called for a player.

highlights.title: Purse planning
highlights.text: Decide a role-wise budget before the first bid is called.

highlights.title: Live bidding
highlights.text: Compete for players in real time against every other table.

highlights.title: Squad balancing
highlights.text: Cover the required roles without overspending the purse.

highlights.title: Squad scoring
highlights.text: Teams are scored on a balanced-squad formula after the auction closes.

events.title: Best Manager
events.short_description: A business simulation in which teams run a fictional company through a busy market.
events.description: Best Manager is a live business simulation. Each team is given a fictional startup with a starting balance sheet and must run it through a compressed market year — pricing, marketing spend, hiring, production capacity and cash flow. Teams make decisions in rounds and submit a short management report after each. The final score combines profitability, market share, employee morale, sustainability and the quality of the team's written reasoning, followed by an interview round for the top teams.
events.eligibility: Open to all students of the participating institution, from any discipline.
events.team_requirements: Teams of two or three with one nominated business manager.
rules: A team must have two or three members and must nominate one business manager.
All monetary figures are virtual; no real money is involved at any stage.
Decisions must be submitted within the round time; late submissions score zero for that round.
Each round's management report must be written by the team members.
Teams may not exchange information with other teams during the simulation.
The final interview is compulsory for teams that qualify for a placing.
Scores are published on the organiser's notice board.

highlights.title: Market decisions
highlights.text: Set prices, choose marketing channels and control production capacity.

highlights.title: Cash flow
highlights.text: Balance hiring, inventory and marketing spend across every round.

highlights.title: Management reporting
highlights.text: Explain each round's decision in a concise written report.

highlights.title: Strategy interview
highlights.text: Defend the final strategy to the judges.

events.title: Debate
events.short_description: A parliamentary debate with constructive speeches, rebuttals and cross-questions.
events.description: Debate puts two teams head to head over a motion announced at the start of the round. The affirmative team presents, the negative team opposes, then both sides receive a rebuttal phase followed by a short cross-question round. Judges assess the quality of arguments, use of evidence, structure, rebuttal strength, clarity of delivery and adherence to the format. Speaking time is strictly enforced.
events.eligibility: Open to all students of the participating institution.
events.team_requirements: Teams of two to four, with a nominated speaker and a nominated rebuttal speaker.
rules: A team must have two to four members, with a nominated speaker and rebuttal speaker.
The motion is announced in advance of the round; teams may prepare notes but not a written speech.
Speaking and rebuttal time are fixed and enforced by the timekeeper.
Points must be relevant to the motion; personal attacks are penalised.
Cross-questioning must be in question form and is limited to the allotted duration.
Reading from a manuscript, slides or a phone is not permitted.
The judges' score sheet with reasons is shared with both teams afterwards.

highlights.title: Team formulation
highlights.text: Agree a core case, the strongest arguments and a rebuttal strategy.

highlights.title: Constructive speeches
highlights.text: Deliver structured opening and supporting arguments.

highlights.title: Rebuttals
highlights.text: Directly dismantle the opposing case with evidence.

highlights.title: Cross questions
highlights.text: Question the other side and expose weak assumptions.

events.title: Reel Making
events.short_description: A short-form video challenge judged on storytelling, editing and sound design.
events.description: Reel Making asks teams to produce an original short-form video on a theme announced on the day. Teams script, shoot, edit and add sound design within the event window. Submissions are judged on storytelling, shot composition, editing rhythm, sound design, originality and how completely the video delivers the theme. A rough cut must be uploaded before the screening slot, followed by a short note from the team about their approach.
events.eligibility: Open to all students of the participating institution.
events.team_requirements: Teams of two to five, covering script, camera, editing and sound roles.
rules: A team must have two to five members and must nominate one director/editor.
The video must be original and must not exceed the published duration limit.
Shooting may only be done on mobile phones.
All footage must be captured within the competition window and in permitted areas.
The video must be uploaded before the screening slot begins.
Only royalty-free or self-recorded audio may be used.
Each team gets one submission; a re-upload is allowed only for a technical error.
Unsafe or hateful content results in immediate disqualification.

highlights.title: Script writing
highlights.text: Shape a short story arc that lands the theme.

highlights.title: Shooting
highlights.text: Plan shots, compose frames and capture clean footage on mobile.

highlights.title: Editing and sound
highlights.text: Cut to rhythm, add titles, music and clean sound design.

highlights.title: Screening
highlights.text: Screen the final cut to the jury and give a director's note.

events.title: Poster Making
events.short_description: A poster contest judged on concept, hierarchy and visual craft.
events.description: Poster Making asks teams to interpret a given theme on a single sheet. Both hand-drawn and digitally produced posters are accepted, and the theme is announced on the spot so no work can be pre-planned. Judges look for a strong single idea, clear visual hierarchy, good use of colour and type, and communication that a passer-by would understand in three seconds. Teams receive a fixed preparation window and must submit the physical or printed sheet at the judging desk.
events.eligibility: Open to all students of the participating institution.
events.team_requirements: Individual entry or a pair. A pair entry counts as one submission.
rules: A team may register individually or as a pair; the entry type must match the registration.
The theme is announced only at the venue, immediately before the preparation window.
Both hand-drawn and digitally created posters are accepted within the published size range.
Only the materials listed in the supplied kit sheet may be used.
The preparation window is strictly timed and monitored.
One submission per team; a re-submission is allowed only for a printing error.
The concept explanation is limited to the published time per team.

highlights.title: Theme interpretation
highlights.text: Read the on-the-spot theme and settle on one clear concept.

highlights.title: Composition
highlights.text: Plan the layout, the focal point and the visual hierarchy.

highlights.title: Execution
highlights.text: Draw or design the poster within the strict time limit.

highlights.title: Concept pitch
highlights.text: Explain the idea behind the poster in one minute.

events.title: Treasure Hunt
events.short_description: A campus-wide scavenger hunt where teams decode clues and race to the final chest.
events.description: Treasure Hunt turns the campus into a game board. Teams receive a sealed clue pack at the starting point and work through checkpoints spread across the site. Clues escalate in difficulty — anagrams, cipher scrambles, logic grids and location riddles — and each solved checkpoint reveals the next. Along the route teams collect bonus tokens for optional mini-challenges, which can be traded for time bonuses. The competition rewards pace, careful reading and coordination between teammates who may never have met before.
events.eligibility: Open to all students of the participating institution.
events.team_requirements: Teams of two to four with a nominated captain.
rules: Teams must consist of two to four members; mixed departments and years are encouraged.
Every team must report to the starting point before the stated time to collect the clue pack.
Clue packs are strictly non-transferable and must stay with the team.
Physical damage to property, or entering restricted areas, results in immediate disqualification.
Bonus tokens can only be redeemed at the published checkpoint and never after it closes.
Teams are expected to maintain sportsmanship; copying another team's route is disqualifying.
Every member must participate in at least the published number of checkpoints.
Ties are resolved by bonus token count and then by finish time.

highlights.title: Clue decoding
highlights.text: Work through anagrams, ciphers and logic grids to unlock the next checkpoint.

highlights.title: Campus navigation
highlights.text: Move between widely separated checkpoints without missing a token.

highlights.title: Team coordination
highlights.text: Assign roles — reader, navigator, solver and runner — under time pressure.

highlights.title: Bonus challenges
highlights.text: Optional side puzzles that convert directly into time and score bonuses.
